candidates: When writing regular expressions, avoid overly broad character class ranges such as `[A-z]`, which inadvertently include non-alphabetic ASCII characters (e.g., `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `_`, `` ` ``); use explicit, tightly scoped ranges such as `[A-Za-z]` or `[A-Z]` and `[a-z]` separately instead.

Shared rendering helpers that must work across multiple diagram types — such as font-icon substitution, math typesetting, or other text-transformation utilities — should be implemented in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/common/common.ts` rather than in individual diagram renderer files, so the capability is uniformly available to every diagram type without duplication.

Heavy optional dependencies should be dynamically imported (`await import(...)`) only when they are actually needed at runtime: gate the import on both the text containing the relevant syntax (e.g., a KaTeX `$$…$$` delimiter check) AND the environment supporting the feature (e.g., `isMathMLSupported() || config.legacyMathML`). Importing at module load time unconditionally inflates the bundle for all users, even those who never use the feature.
Do not include unrelated whitespace, indentation, or formatting changes in a feature PR; revert them or move them to a separate dedicated clean-up PR so the diff remains focused on the stated change.

In documentation source files under `packages/mermaid/src/docs/`, version-gated feature headings must use the placeholder `(v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)` rather than a hardcoded version number — this placeholder is automatically substituted with the actual release version by the docs build pipeline that publishes content to the `docs/` directory.
